metadata.abstract: We organize an exploratory study of exact prime counting in the classical computational model. No fixed-power improvement over square-root time is obtained, either unconditionally or under the Riemann hypothesis. We give exponent-preserving reductions between pi(N) modulo 3 and the ternary divisor summatory function modulo 9, precision-lifting identities, and obstructions for specified coefficient and carry representations. A bounded local zeta representation permits controlled logarithm expansion and direct oscillatory integration. Cardinal B-spline windows reduce the required output to a polylogarithmic number of resonant frequencies, which can be extracted using a marked rational-function algorithm. The current aggregate cost remains essentially linear in integration height. A provisional time-space combination is explicitly separated from established results and implemented algorithms. Reference programs and finite validation accompany the note; they do not establish asymptotic performance or interval-certified prime counting.

agents.role: Literature checking, exploratory mathematics, reference-code preparation, and manuscript drafting

metadata.title: Exact Prime Counting at the Square-Root Scale: Modular Reductions and Direct Local Integration
